title: The Battle Before The Battle
subtitle: When Bad News Stops Traveling Upward
tagline: If telling the leader the truth consistently costs something, eventually the leader will be surrounded by people who tell him what he wants to hear.
headline: Why Leaders Stop Hearing Bad News
headline_sub: Are You Surrounded by Peace, or Silence?
seo_title: Why Leaders Stop Hearing Bad News | TheWrkShop
seo_description: When telling the leader the truth costs something, people stop telling it. A biblical look at how leaders lose honest information at work, on teams and at home.
og_image_alt: Why Leaders Stop Hearing Bad News: When truth becomes expensive, information becomes distorted. TheWrkShop, Leadership & Culture.

scriptures.text: The king of Israel answered Jehoshaphat, “There is still one prophet through whom we can inquire of the LORD, but I hate him because he never prophesies anything good about me, but always bad. He is Micaiah son of Imlah.”

blocks.text: Ahab says something extraordinary.
There is a man who may tell him the truth.
And Ahab’s response is essentially:
“I DON’T LIKE HIM.”
Why?
Because Micaiah doesn’t tell him what he wants to hear.
Think about that organizationally.
But the king’s hostility toward unwelcome information creates a dangerous environment.
Eventually people learn:
GOOD NEWS TRAVELS SAFELY. BAD NEWS DOESN’T.
That’s how leaders become blind while remaining completely in charge.
“IF SOMETHING WERE REALLY WRONG, SOMEBODY WOULD TELL ME.”
Would they?
What happened the last time someone brought you bad news?
Did you:
Because people remember.
And then:
THE ORGANIZATION LEARNS YOUR EMOTIONAL PRICE FOR TRUTH.
Eventually information gets edited before it reaches you.
LEADERS NEED PEOPLE WHO CAN INTERRUPT THEIR VERSION OF REALITY.
People who can say:

items: “The numbers aren’t telling the whole story.”

blocks.text: And:
“I THINK YOU’RE WRONG.”
A leader who cannot receive those sentences eventually becomes dependent upon incomplete information.
Watch the progression:

steps: Leader makes decisions from distorted reality.
blocks.caption: They may have learned not to.

items: WHAT INFORMATION AM I LEAST LIKELY TO HEAR?
WHO CAN TELL ME SOMETHING I DON’T WANT TO HEAR?
WHAT HAPPENS TO PEOPLE WHO DISAGREE WITH ME?
DO PEOPLE BRING ME PROBLEMS EARLY OR WAIT UNTIL THEY’RE UNAVOIDABLE?
HAVE I CONFUSED LOYALTY WITH AGREEMENT?

blocks.text: Then:
AM I SURROUNDED BY PEACE, OR SILENCE?
Those are not necessarily the same thing.
Ask someone with enough proximity to know:
“WHAT DO YOU THINK PEOPLE ARE AFRAID TO TELL ME?”
Then do something difficult.
Because if truth reaches you safely today, it may reach you sooner tomorrow.
When truth becomes expensive, information becomes distorted.
Father,
Protect me from becoming hostile toward truth because truth makes me uncomfortable.

items: And give me humility to listen to them.
Make me secure enough to hear bad news.

blocks.text: Don’t let my authority isolate me from reality.
When truth becomes expensive, information becomes distorted.
People learn the emotional price a leader charges for truth.
Leaders need people who can interrupt their version of reality.
Authority without honest information creates confident blindness.
Have I confused loyalty with agreement?
Am I surrounded by peace, or silence?
